title: The Impact of Culture on Knowledge Acquisition and Innovation Processes in Companies/Countries Towards Sustainable Development. Empirical Research Based on International Rankings
content: In the current social-economic context, most companies and countries in the world, including EU Member States, are adopting strategies/policies to improve their competitive position at international level. The aim of the present study is to argue, on the basis of quantitative research, that education has become the essential vector for knowledge acquisition and continuous innovation, as well as for sustainable development and the achievement of some SDGs goals. At the core of the study is an informal, cross-case analysis between some rankings for companies (e.g. BCG) versus some rankings for countries (e.g. LPI) in order to infer/deduce to what extent the values/culture for each of the two categories of entities influence socially performing behavior. In essence, the result of our study shows that each individual's general education as well as continuous learning as a member of an organization/society directly condition the acquisition of new knowledge, continuous innovation and sustainable development at the level of any hierarchically structured social group. Our study brings some elements of absolute novelty in management and sociology (e.g.: the identification of systemic trust and tacit knowledge as common organizational vs. national values; the synergy effect of teams through the application of Ba, etc.) that are of both conceptual and pragmatic interest.
